To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the timbre-words used by musicians can be used to describe timbral characteristics of synthesized sounds and (2) timbre-words are not always used in a consistent way by musicians.

(1) the timbre-words of a musician can be used to control synthesis, (2) timbral control is possible with both neural networks and genetic algorithms, (3) the timbre of a sound is not a single characteristic, but a combination of several characteristics, (4) the timbral characteristics of a sound can be recognised and manipulated independently from each other, (5) the timbre characteristics of a sound are not static but depend on the context of the sound, and

we have developed a system that can (1) recognise timbral characteristics using a genetic algorithm, (2) recognise timbral adjectives and adverb using a genetic algorithm and (3) adjust the timbral characteristics of a sound using a genetic algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of interfaces to synthesis algorithms which will allow us to specify the desired sound by describing its timbre.
the problem of how to build interfaces that will allow us as humans to communicate with computers using timbre-words, and how to build synthesis algorithms that can respond to timbre-words.
the following questions: How can we recognise timbral characteristics? How can we adjust timbral characteristics?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work shows the potential for using genetic algorithms and neural network methods to recognise timbre-words and to manipulate timbre, but that there is still much work to be done to make these methods useful in practice.
we are still a long way from being able to provide interfaces to synthesis that are as flexible and expressive as the timbre-words used by musicians to describe and manipulate timbre.
we have not yet achieved our goal, but we are getting there, and we can see the way ahead.

we are trying to develop a new way to communicate about timbral characteristics of sounds, and to manipulate timbre in real time.
we have developed a system which allows the user to specify timbral characteristics of a sound by using a set of adjectives, and then the system can generate sounds that match those adjectives.
we are trying to learn to recognise timbre and to control timbre.

it is possible to create interfaces for manipulating timbre directly using timbre-words.
timbre-words are useful for communicating about timbre.
timbre is not a property of sounds, but a property of listeners' perceptions of sounds.
